description: Work vessels at Berth 1 and Berth 2: crane work queues, container moves, lashing, tally and completion messages to carriers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A vessel call has a fixed berth window of about 18 to 30 hours; a missed window delays the carrier service and the next call. Container location and hazardous cargo stowage data must be current to load safely. About $77K average revenue per day, much of it earned on vessel days
manual_workaround: Paper bay plans and load lists from the carrier; crane work queues run by radio from the shift superintendent; tally on paper; reconcile in the TOS after recovery. Workable for about one shift at reduced productivity
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-03; SYS-05; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-10
dependent_third_parties: Ocean carriers; longshore hiring hall; crane vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vessel planners; shift superintendents; longshore labor; Berth 1 and Berth 2

description: In-gate and out-gate for about 800 truck transactions a day: TWIC check, OCR of container, chassis and plate, appointment and customs hold check, interchange receipt
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Trucks queue on port roads within about 2 hours of a gate stop. Releasing a container that is on a customs hold is a regulatory failure, so the gate must stop rather than guess. TOS gate transactions must not be lost (RPO 1 h)
manual_workaround: Manual gate: clerks key container numbers on a printed release list, TWIC checked by security officers, paper interchange receipts; lanes cut from 3 to 1 and import deliveries limited to containers confirmed released
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-07; SYS-08
dependent_third_parties: Trucking companies; customs data exchange service; OCR vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Gate and yard clerks; security officers; gate complex

description: Container inventory and location, RTG and yard tractor dispatch through VMTs, reefer plug monitoring (300 plugs), and equipment moves between berth, yard and gate
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without current locations, containers are lost in the stacks and moves slow sharply. Reefers must be checked by hand every 4 hours when monitoring is down. Yard data can be rebuilt from a physical yard check, but that takes 1 to 2 shifts
manual_workaround: Printed yard inventory from the last export; radio dispatch; manual reefer checks every 4 hours by the reefer mechanic; physical yard check if data is lost
dependent_third_parties: Crane vendor; VMT and Wi-Fi support (MSP)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Yard clerks; RTG and yard tractor operators; reefer mechanics

description: TWIC-based access to secure areas, CCTV, security patrols, and the dangerous cargo location list used by the FSO and emergency responders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Emergency responders must be able to find hazardous cargo at any time; FSP access control must continue at every MARSEC level (33 CFR Part 105). A failure could contribute to a transportation security incident
manual_workaround: Security officers check TWIC visually and log entries by hand; printed dangerous cargo location list from each shift (to be introduced; see P01 R-030); CCTV recorders keep recording locally if the network is down
dependent_third_parties: Port authority police and fire; Captain of the Port
dependent_people_or_facilities: Security officers; FSO; gate complex and yard

business_process: Customs status and carrier EDI exchange
description: Receive release and hold status from the customs data exchange; exchange bay plans, load and discharge lists and container status with 6 carrier services; vessel schedules and gate status with the port community system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Holds and releases change during the day and drive the gate. Partners can resend the last 24 hours of messages, so data loss is recoverable, but an unreliable hold status stops import deliveries
manual_workaround: Check hold status through the customs data exchange web portal; carriers email bay plans and lists; port community system updated through its web screens
dependent_third_parties: Ocean carriers; customs data exchange service; port community system (port authority)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vessel planners; gate clerks; customer service

description: Berth scheduling, stowage and crane split planning, yard allocation, and the advisory scheduling optimization pilot
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plans are prepared 24 to 72 hours before a vessel arrives, so planning can pause for a day. Wrong stowage of heavy or hazardous containers is a safety issue, so plans made by hand need a second planner check
manual_workaround: Plan on carrier-supplied bay plans and spreadsheets; berth schedule kept on the whiteboard and shared by email and phone; the optimization service is not needed (planners plan by hand today)

business_process: Crane and equipment maintenance and OT support
description: Maintain STS cranes, the mobile harbor crane, RTGs, reach stackers and yard tractors; manage PLC and HMI programs and vendor diagnostics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cranes run on local controllers and can work without the TOS, but a crane with a corrupted PLC program cannot work at all and each STS crane carries about half of Berth 1 capacity. PLC programs change rarely, so the RPO is the last approved program version (at most 24 h of change)
manual_workaround: Operate cranes in local mode with operators in the cab; isolate the crane network; vendor technician on site to reload controller programs from vendor copies
dependent_people_or_facilities: Mechanics and crane electricians; crane electrical houses

description: Truck appointment and customer portal (hosted by the TOS vendor), container availability inquiries, email and phone service to carriers, trucking companies and cargo owners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Truckers need appointments and availability to plan the next day. Appointments can be taken by phone and email for one day
manual_workaround: Phone and email appointments recorded on a shared spreadsheet; availability list emailed to trucking companies twice a day
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-06; TOS vendor hosted portal

description: Vessel and cargo handling invoices to carriers, demurrage and storage charges, hosted payment page for truckers and cargo owners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Billing can wait about 72 hours; charges are rebuilt from TOS move history. Cash impact grows after a week
manual_workaround: Queue invoices; rebuild charges from TOS move history after recovery; collect by check or the payment service provider

description: Employee payroll, timekeeping, onboarding and termination, accounts payable
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; missing it has legal and retention impact. Longshore labor is paid through the hiring hall process, not company payroll
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper timesheets
